label: Matrix Properties and Decompositions
notes: This appendix is the linear-algebra toolbox standing behind every camera, epipole, homography, and tensor estimate in the book. Across these ten printed pages we tour the SVD, eigen and Cholesky factorizations, and the QR and RQ decompositions, treating each one as a geometric act on vectors rather than a recipe.

label: Rank and Null Space
notes: Rank counts the independent columns, while the null space collects every direction the matrix annihilates. In vision these are not abstractions: a homogeneous solution is a null vector, and a constraint matrix that should be rank deficient announces estimable structure exactly when its smallest singular value drops toward zero.

label: The Singular Value Decomposition
notes: Every real matrix factors as a rotation, an axis-aligned scaling, and another rotation. The singular values are the scale factors along the principal axes. This rotate-scale-rotate picture is the single most useful mental model in the appendix, because it reduces an opaque matrix to three geometric moves.

label: Null Space from the SVD
notes: When we minimize the norm of A x subject to unit x, the answer is the last column of V, the right singular vector with the smallest singular value. Almost every linear estimator in the course, from the DLT homography to the fundamental matrix, ends with exactly this one line.

label: Low-Rank Approximation
notes: Zeroing the smallest singular values gives the closest rank r matrix in Frobenius and spectral norm, the Eckart and Young theorem. This is how we force the fundamental matrix to rank two and how noisy measurement or track matrices are cleaned by discarding the singular values that merely encode noise.

label: Eigen-decomposition and Symmetry
notes: A symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and an orthonormal eigenbasis, so it diagonalizes by a rotation. Positive definiteness means every eigenvalue is strictly positive, which is what makes a covariance matrix valid and a conic a genuine ellipse rather than a degenerate or imaginary curve.

label: QR and RQ Decomposition
notes: QR writes a matrix as an orthogonal factor times upper triangular; RQ reverses the order to upper triangular times orthogonal. RQ is the one we want for cameras, because the calibration matrix is upper triangular and the orientation is a rotation, matching the physical structure of a finite projective camera.

label: Factoring the Camera P
notes: The left three by three block of a finite camera is calibration times rotation. RQ recovers both: K is the upper-triangular intrinsics and R is the rotation. We fix signs so the focal lengths are positive and the determinant of R equals one, then read the centre from the remaining column.

label: Cholesky and the Absolute Conic
notes: A positive definite matrix factors as a lower triangular times its transpose. Applied to the image of the absolute conic, Cholesky extracts the calibration directly: omega equals K inverse transpose times K inverse, so factoring omega and inverting gives K without ever decomposing a full camera matrix.

label: Pseudo-inverse and Conditioning
notes: The pseudo-inverse inverts the nonzero singular values and solves least squares; the back-projection of an image point through a camera uses it directly. The condition number, the ratio of largest to smallest singular value, predicts how measurement noise is amplified, which is why data normalization matters so much in practice.

label: Skew-Symmetric Matrices
notes: The cross product a cross b equals the skew matrix of a times b. That skew matrix is rank two, and its one-dimensional null space is the vector a itself. This is the algebra behind epipolar lines, the essential matrix, and triangulation constraints written as vanishing cross products.

label: Toolbox Recap
notes: Hold on to the rotate-scale-rotate picture of the SVD, the last column of V as a null space, rank-r truncation as the closest low-rank matrix, RQ as the camera factorization, and Cholesky as the route from omega to K. Each decomposition turns a matrix back into geometry you can reason about.
